courses.title: Social and Ethical Issues in Computing
courses.description: History, social context and methods and tools of analysis. Professional and ethical responsibilities. Intellectual property. Privacy and civil liberties.

courses.title: AI-Assisted Data Science for Non-Scientists
courses.description: In today’s digital era, data is omnipresent. Every day, we answer questions and make tough decisions based on data. Whether in business, healthcare, humanities, or any other domain, understanding data to draw insights and make informed decisions from data can be a game-changer. This course demystiﬁes data science by showing what data science can do for you. In the age of AI, that means putting the tools to actually do it within your reach without ﬁrst learning to program or mastering the underlying mathematics. MTH 099.

courses.title: Data Science for the World
courses.description: Introduction to the concepts of data science. Basic data analysis skills. The programming language R. Lecture 3 hours, laboratory 2 hours.

courses.title: Python Programming for Everyone
courses.description: Introduction to computing, programming, and Python. Data and variables. Control flow. Methods. Arrays and lists. Object oriented programming. Lecture 2 hours, laboratory 2 hours. Pre/Corequisite: MTH 107, or Math SAT score of 620, or ACT score of 27, or ALEKS score of 61.

courses.title: Cybersecurity: An Introduction to Security in Cyberspace
courses.description: An introduction to cybersecurity. Recent incidents. The Internet. Types of attacks. Tools for defending against attacks on users and networks. Legal, moral, and social aspects.

courses.title: Information Technology and Society
courses.description: A variety of topics on information technology and society through various course activities including research papers, experiments, and by reading articles. The topics covered include but are not limited to: history of computing, hardware mechanisms, algorithms design, software development principles, software tools, security, and artiﬁcial intelligence.

courses.title: Computers and Society
courses.description: Basic concepts of computer systems. Installing, conﬁguring, and managing computer software. Internet information retrieval. Application software. HTML, programming for the www in JavaScript. E-commerce, cryptography, computer security. Social, legal, ethical issues and the future.

courses.title: Computer Programming I
courses.description: History of computing. Fundamental programming constructs. Algorithms and problem solving. Object-oriented programming. Recursion. Lecture 2 hours, laboratory 2 hours.
courses.requisites: CSC115 or BTE320 or MTH141 or MTH151 or MTH161 or MTH171 or MAS110.

courses.title: AI For Me: In School, In Work, In Life
courses.description: AI for Me is a hands-on, introductory course that explores how cutting-edge artiﬁcial intelligence tools can enhance your academic, professional, and personal life. You'll learn how AI works, where it came from, and why it matters. From using AI to write papers, build resumes, or prepare presentations, to analyzing data, creating digital art, or exploring hobbies, this course shows how AI can help you do things better, faster, and smarter. Whether you're looking to boost your grades, level up your LinkedIn, or just planning your Spring Break, AI for Me unleashes the power of AI in a practical

courses.title: Introductory Topics in Computer Science
courses.description: Freshman topics in Computer Science - Content varies by semester.

courses.title: Computing for Scientists
courses.description: Introduction to computing. Computing applications in science. Tools for applications. Algorithms for applications. Implementation of algorithms. Data in science. Storage and retrieval of data. Analysis and visualization of data.
courses.requisites: MTH 141 or MTH 151 or MTH 161 or MTH 171.

courses.title: Computer Programming II
courses.description: Common APIs including list, priority queue, set, and map, and their efﬁcient implementations in an object-oriented language using fundamental data structures. Sorting and other applications of recursion. Combining asymptotic analysis and experiments to extrapolate running times. Using APIs in a software project. Lecture 3 hours, laboratory 2 hours.
courses.requisites: CSC 120 or BTE 324 or ECE 218 and MTH 108 or MTH 140 or MTH 141 or MTH 161 or MTH 162 or MTH 171 or MTH 172 or MAS 110.

courses.title: Sophomore Topics in Computer Science
courses.description: Sophomore Topics in Computer Science - Content varies by semester.

courses.title: Computer Organization and Architecture
courses.description: Digital logic and digital systems. Machine level representation of data. Assembly level machine organization. Memory system organization and architecture. Interfacing and communication. Functional organization. Multiprocessing and alternative architectures.
courses.requisites: CSC 120. or BTE 324. or ECE 218. and Corequisite: MTH 309 or MTH 230.

courses.title: Introduction to Python for Scientists
courses.description: Python programming. Python packages for scientiﬁc applications. Data science and machine learning applications. Designed for students from the sciences.
courses.requisites: MTH 161 and (CSC113 or MTH224 or other approved statistics course).

courses.title: Data Structures and Algorithm Analysis
courses.description: Basic algorithmic analysis. Algorithmic strategies. Fundamental computing algorithms. Distributed algorithms. Cryptographic algorithms. Geometric algorithms.
courses.requisites: CSC 220 or ECE 318 , and MTH 309 or MTH 230.

courses.title: System Programming
courses.description: Using UNIX: User environment, Shells, File system, Tools, Scripting. C programming: Core language elements, Pointers, Libraries, Tools, Programming for UNIX: System calls, System information, Processes and threads, File system, Signals, Interfaces to the internet.

courses.title: Introduction to Game Programming
courses.description: Fundamental programming issues in game design: Software design; Version control; Basic graphics; GUI programming. Large-scale game project: Team development of a functional game; Graphics and GUI component; Networking component; Core game engine.

courses.title: Android Programming
courses.description: The Android Studio programming environment. The Android execution model. User interfaces. Media. Data storage areas. Sensors and actuators.

courses.title: Introduction to Artiﬁcial Intelligence
courses.description: What is AI? Input. Knowledge representation. Learning. Reasoning. Output. Ethics. Future of AI. (CSC220 or ECE318), MTH161, (MTH309 or MTH230).

courses.description: Junior Topics in Computer Science - Content varies by semester.

courses.title: Computer Science Practicum II
courses.description: Implementation of techniques, algorithms, and data structures being taught in a co-requisite computer science course.

courses.title: Computer Science Practicum III

courses.title: Computer Science Seminars Reports
courses.description: A range of topics in Computer Science, as embodied in the seminars hosted by the Department. Students write reports about the seminars.
courses.requisites: At least 12 credits of CSC courses.

courses.title: Computer Science Project Planning
courses.description: Planning for the implementation of a Computer Science project, including: Problem analysis, System architecture design, Algorithm and data structure selection, User interface design, Veriﬁcation and validation plan, and Prototyping.
courses.requisites: At least 12 credits of CSC courses.

courses.title: Computer Science Project Implementation
courses.description: Implementation of a Computer Science project, including: Hardware preparation, Component implementation, System integration, Veriﬁcation and validation, and Documentation.
courses.requisites: At least 12 credits of CSC courses.

courses.title: Computer Science Internship
courses.description: A commercial computing environment. Normally 50 internship hours are required per credit earned (the host company must supply documentary evidence of hours worked).
courses.requisites: At least 12 credits of CSC courses.

courses.title: Programming Languages
courses.description: Overview of programming languages. Fundamental issues in language design. Virtual machines. Introduction to language translation. Models of execution control. Declaration, modularity, and storage management. Programming language semantics. Programming paradigms.

courses.title: Principles of Computer Operating Systems
courses.description: Process management. Scheduling and dispatch. Interprocess communication. Memory management. File systems. Device management. Security and protection. System programming for UNIX.

courses.title: Database Systems
courses.description: Information models and systems. Database systems. Data modeling. Relational databases. Relational database design. Database query languages, Data mining concepts, Web database programming.

courses.title: Computer Networks
courses.description: Introduction to computer networks and network applications. The protocol stack. Routing, switching and bridging technologies. Models of network computing. Internet standards and protocols.

courses.title: Theory of Computing
courses.description: Sets, relations, and languages. Automata theory. Basic computability theory. Turing machines. The complexity classes P and NP.
courses.requisites: CSC 220 or ECE 318 , and MTH 309 or MTH 230.

courses.title: Introduction to Software Engineering
courses.description: Software processes, requirements and speciﬁcations, design, validation, evolution. Project management, tools and environments. Foundations of human-computer interaction. Risks and liabilities of computer-based systems. Intellectual property.

courses.title: Teaching Assistant Training in Computer Science
courses.description: Training and teaching assistant for a speciﬁc course, in computer laboratories. May be taken multiple times, assisting maximally twice for a given course.
courses.requisites: At least 12 credits of CSC courses.

courses.description: Senior Topics in Computer Science - content varies by semester.
courses.requisites: At least 12 credits of CSC courses.

courses.title: Logic and Automated Reasoning
courses.description: Propositional and ﬁrst order logic. Reasoning and resolution. More complex inference rules. Proof search reﬁnements. Gödel's incompleteness theorem. Using contemporary Automated Theorem Proving (ATP) systems. Applications of ATP in research and industry.
courses.requisites: CSC317 or CSC545 and MTH309 or MTH230.

courses.title: Data Security and Cryptography
courses.description: Access, information flow, and inference controls. Network security and management. Encryption algorithms. Cryptographic techniques.

courses.title: Cybersecurity
courses.description: Introduction to Cyberspace. Foundations of Cybersecurity. Blockchain and its applications. Malware and counter measures against malware. Firewalls. Intrusion detection and prevention systems. Security for cloud computing and the Internet of Things. Design and implementation of secure software systems.

courses.title: Interpreters and Compiler Theory
courses.description: Translation of higher-level languages into machine language. Grammars, parsing, scanners, precedence relations. Run-time storage and symbol table organization. Semantic routines. Chaining and hashing. Code generation and optimization. Macro implementation.

courses.title: Introduction to Parallel Computing
courses.description: Parallel computing systems. Shared-memory parallel programming, with Open-MP. Distributed-memory parallel programming, with Open-MPI. Applications: Vector and matrix operations, sorting, image processing.

courses.title: Introduction to Computer Graphics
courses.description: Geometric objects and transformations. Lighting and shading. Texture mapping. Modeling and hierarchy. Advanced rendering techniques. Graphics card architecture, OpenGL, fragment shader and vertex shader language.

courses.title: Algorithm Design and Analysis
courses.description: Design techniques, including divide-and-conquer, greedy method, dynamic programming, backtracking. Time and space complexity. Sorting and searching. Combinatorial and graph algorithms.

courses.title: Statistical Learning with Applications
courses.description: Supervised and unsupervised learning. Regression and classiﬁcation. Statistical learning methods: K-Nearest Neighbors, linear models, tree-based methods, support vector machines. Dimensionality reduction and clustering. Applications of statistical learning methods using R.

courses.title: Computer Vision with Deep Learning
courses.description: The purpose of this course is to learn about computer vision using Deep Learning. Deep Learning is the technology that powers the most recent generation of Artiﬁcial Intelligence systems including the recent large-scale generative models. In this course, we will use Deep Learning to process, analyze and generate images. This is a project-driven course. There will be two programming projects, and a semester long term project. Students will propose their own topic for the term project. All assignments will be completed using the Pytorch library.

courses.title: Introduction to Artiﬁcial Intelligence
courses.description: Fundamental issues in intelligent systems. Search and constraint satisfaction. Knowledge representation and reasoning. Natural language processing. Machine learning and neural networks. Game theory. AI programming.
courses.requisites: CSC 317 or ECE 511, MTH 224 or ECE 310 or IEN 310.

courses.title: Introduction to Machine Learning with Applications
courses.description: Python and probability, the Numpy package. K-means clustering. The Gaussian mixture model. Kernel density estimation. Dimensionality reduction. Classiﬁcation. Regression, SVM, and SVR. Ensemble learning. Cross validation for model selection. Signal encoding-decoding. Dictionary learning. Metrics for performance evaluation. Deep neural networks. Neural networks, the Pytorch and Keras packages. Computational graph and automatic differentiation. Convolutional neural networks. Autoencoders. Generative adversarial networks. Transfer learning.

courses.title: Computational Geometry
courses.description: Algorithms for solving geometric problems arising from application domains including graphics, robotics, and GIS.

courses.title: Problem Solving for Bioinformatics
courses.description: Grand challenges, solutions, and emerging opportunities in bioinformatics. PERL programming from the most basic to advanced contents such as multidimensional array, regular expression, hash, and sorting. Theories and hands-on projects in 3D genome structure inference, protein secondary structure prediction, protein tertiary structure prediction, protein model quality assessment, protein function prediction, and biological network analysis. Analysis of real-world biomedical data. Applications of machine learning algorithms.

courses.title: Biomedical Data Science
courses.description: The computational skills needed for analysis of genomic and biomedical data sets, including: The basics of a command line interface; programming in (bio-)python; running programs on Pegasus2; writing scripts for downloading, manipulating, and analyzing data; ﬁle sharing and version control using github; analyzing a Next Generation Sequencing data set, and interpreting the results; and responsible conduct of Research.

courses.title: Computational Neuroscience
courses.description: Introduction to computational neuroscience. Analysis and modeling of neural systems. Neurons, populations of neurons, perception, behavior. Connections to machine learning. Tutorials in Matlab.

courses.title: Bioinformatics Tools
courses.description: Databases and tools of bioinformatics, as relevant to research in genomics and molecular biology. Bioinformatics applications. Information retrieval, analytical tools, BLAST searches, promoter analysis, and protein structure- function analysis, and various applications.

courses.title: Multimedia Systems
courses.description: Speciﬁcation and requirements of a multimedia hardware system. Multimedia data technologies. Graphics ﬁle formats. Compression and decompression. Multimedia application development.

courses.title: Computer Science Graduate Internship
courses.description: This course monitors students doing an internship in a professional computer science environment. The exact nature of the course will be dependent on the nature of the internship and the requirements of the host organizations. Normally 50 internship hours are required per credit earned (the host organization must supply documentary evidence of hours worked).
courses.requisites: Students must complete at least 18 credits prior to enrolling in the internship course.

courses.title: Mobile Wireless Systems
courses.description: Cellular Systems, multiple access techniques, wireless networking, mobile IP, power management, user location information management, TDMA, CDMA, and GSM systems, data broadcasting.

courses.title: Theory of Computation
courses.description: Recursive functions, Markov algorithms, Turing machines. Unsolvability.

courses.title: Parallel Algorithms
courses.description: Parallel computation models. Sorting networks. Parallel algorithms for sorting, searching, graph problems, preﬁx computation, pattern matching, and fast Fourier transforms. Theory of P-completeness. The class NC.

courses.title: Neural Networks and Deep Learning
courses.description: Fundamentals of artiﬁcial neural networks: Perceptrons, Single-layer perceptron classiﬁers, Multi-Layer feedforward networks, Error back-propagation training. Deep Feedforward Networks: Regularization for deep learning, Optimization for training deep models, Convolution networks. Applications: Computer vision, speech recognition, Natural language processing.

courses.title: Complexity Theory
courses.description: Models of computations, Blum's axioms, intractability, NP-completeness.

courses.title: Automated Reasoning
courses.description: Propositional and 1st order logic. Reasoning and resolution. More complex inference rules. Using contemporary ATP systems. Prolog as an ATP system and as a programming language. Applications of ATP in research and industry.

courses.title: Semantic Web
courses.description: An overview of the underlying semantic web technologies. Ontology construction and implementation using tools and APIs (logic, XML, RDF, RDFS). Theoretical and practical aspects of knowledge representation (description logic, RDF, RDFS, SPARQL, SROIQ(D)). Designing and debugging ontologies (ontology engineering, entailment tools, project).

courses.title: Autonomous Robotic Systems
courses.description: Introduction: autonomous systems, autonomous robots, RoboCup, typical components of an autonomous robot. Modeling: perception, noise, modeling, recursive state estimation, Bayes' ﬁlter, particle ﬁlter, self-localization. Control and motion: PID-control, calibration of parameters, controlling a wheeled robot, controlling joints, walking motion. Learning (optional, if time permits): overview, different types of learning, reinforcement learning.
